newsitem.title: UK: LME copper puts on another spurt, still nervous.
newsitem.headline: LME copper puts on another spurt, still nervous.

text.p: Copper prices snapped higher again in late inter-office trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday as nervousness ahead of Wednesday's September options declaration persisted.
At 1800 GMT three month copper futures were last quoted at $2,065/70 a tonne against $2,040 at the afternoon kerb close.
Cash was steady at around $30 above three month values.
September copper prices were indicated at just below $2,100, one of the key strike prices for the September declaration.
But after renewed volatility this week, dealers were not ruling out another spike towards $2,200 in the very short term.
Support was pegged at $1,970, Tuesday's low.
Other base metals were little changed to slightly higher than Tuesday's afternoon kerb closing levels.
